football_evidence.question: Can Coastal Carolina’s pass rush get to Georgia State’s quarterback?
football_evidence.assessment: Some measured evidence supports EdgeDesk’s lean toward Georgia State, and its own breakdown accounts for about 1.1 of the 4.2 points, but not the full gap. It is a research question, not a bet.
supporting: When Georgia State has the ball (the passing game against the pass defense): Georgia State’s offense averages 8.7 yards per pass attempt, and Coastal Carolina’s defense allows 9.1 yards per pass attempt (FBS average 7.4).

When Georgia State has the ball (big plays through the air): Georgia State’s offense turns 15.7% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Coastal Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 14.5% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Georgia State has the ball (big plays on the ground): Georgia State’s offense turns 7.9% of its runs into explosive gains, and Coastal Carolina’s defense gives up explosive gains on 9.1% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Coastal Carolina has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Coastal Carolina’s offense has allowed a sack on 9.3% of its dropbacks, and Georgia State’s defense sacks the quarterback on 11.5% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
contradicting: When Coastal Carolina has the ball (big plays through the air): Coastal Carolina’s offense turns 13.3% of its pass plays into explosive gains, and Georgia State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 11.3% of opponent pass plays (FBS average 10.2%).

When Coastal Carolina has the ball (big plays on the ground): Coastal Carolina’s offense turns 6.7% of its runs into explosive gains, and Georgia State’s defense gives up explosive gains on 8.9% of opponent runs (FBS average 6.5%).

When Georgia State has the ball (pass protection against the pass rush): Georgia State’s offense has allowed a sack on 3.2% of its dropbacks, and Coastal Carolina’s defense sacks the quarterback on 9.6% of opponent dropbacks (FBS average 5.7%).
In his last two games (James Madison and Arkansas State), Brown averaged 5.7 yards per attempt, against 8.9 in his five games before that.
quarterbacks: Cameran Brown has completed 108 of 164 passes (65.9%) for 1,342 yards, 8.2 yards per attempt, 14 touchdowns and 5 interceptions in seven games for Georgia State, and has been sacked on 6 of 170 dropbacks.
Ayden Pereira has completed 23 of 38 passes (60.5%) for 277 yards, 7.3 yards per attempt, 2 touchdowns and 3 interceptions in six games for Georgia State, and has been sacked on 1 of 39 dropbacks.

Deuce Bailey has completed 109 of 205 passes (53.2%) for 1,650 yards, 8.0 yards per attempt, 16 touchdowns and 4 interceptions in seven games for Coastal Carolina, and has been sacked on 18 of 223 dropbacks.
